summary: Scholarship from the Beijing municipal government for non-Chinese citizens studying at higher education institutions and research institutes in Beijing, for degree and non-degree students. Applicants apply through the host institution, which reviews applications and selects recipients. Age limits at enrolment: bachelor's 25, master's 35, doctoral 40, preparatory 24, visiting students 45, research scholars 50. Chinese-taught degree programmes need HSK 4; English-taught Category A needs TOEFL 85 or IELTS 6.5. Category A generally requires a top-500 QS university or key senior secondary school and an average of 85 or GPA 3.6; Categories B and C an average of 80 or GPA 3.0. Master's, doctoral and research-scholar applicants need two recommendation letters from associate professors or higher. Recipients cannot hold other Chinese government or institutional scholarships at the same time, apart from one-off awards.
source_publisher: International Web Portal of Beijing (Beijing Municipal Government)

summary: English-taught programme in China for the Class of 2028-2029, starting August 2028. Applicants must be at least 18 and under 29 on 1 August 2028 and hold, or be on track to complete before that date, an undergraduate degree in any field. Non-native English speakers need test scores (TOEFL iBT 100, IELTS 7, Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185, Duolingo 130) unless they studied in English for at least two years. The application asks for a CV, a 750-word leadership essay, a 500-word statement of purpose, official transcripts, three recommendation letters and a one-minute video. Interviews are held in late October and early November. Some universities set internal deadlines.
deadline_source_text: Application period April to September 2027 for U.S. and Global applicants (selection October to November 2027) and March to May 2027 for applicants with Chinese citizenship. The page gives no exact dates or time zone.
